title: Speck - SynSense
summary: The Speck is a fully event-driven neuromorphic vision System-on-Chip (SoC) developed by Zurich-based startup SynSense AG. It integrates a dynamic vision sensor with an asynchronous architecture supporting up to 328K spiking neurons and nine configurable convolutional layers for sparse, in-memory computing. The chip achieves ultra-low power consumption below one milliwatt while processing single events at approximately 3.36 microseconds latency using networks like LeNet or ResNet. Designed specifically for edge applications such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, and IoT devices, the hardware interfaces with SynSense's SINABS software framework to convert standard deep learning models into spiking convolutional neural network equivalents.
tldr: SynSense AG developed Speck, an ultra-low power neuromorphic vision SoC integrating a dynamic sensor for real-time event-driven processing in edge applications like robotics and autonomous vehicles.
evidence: Speck is a fully event-driven neuromorphic vision SoC.
The Speck chip contains 328K spiking integrate-and-fire neurons.
It utilizes in-memory computing techniques to perform sparse, event-driven neural network computations, enabling extremely low power consumption in the sub-milliwatt range.
For classical applications, Speck can provide intelligence upon the scene at only mWs with a latency of 3.36us for a single event processed by a 9 layer network.
